column3: “Full” and “for himself” make implications explicit rather than translating separate words.
The Greek explicitly says he breathed his last; “what had happened” supplies the unstated object of hearing.
“His body” makes the Greek pronoun explicit.
“You and your husband” expands the Greek plural “you.”
The critical text has no verb of saying here; BSB supplies “replied,” as the Textus Receptus has “said” (εἶπεν). “Also” at the end is supplied.
The Greek describes signs happening through the apostles’ hands and all being together; BSB supplies “the believers” and makes performing active.
BSB moves the contrast about popular esteem before the statement about outsiders.
“They went out” renders the Greek rising clause, which appears before their jealousy.
“Courts,” “full message,” and “new” expand the Greek “all the words of this life.”
“The apostles,” “courts,” “as they had been told,” and “began” make the Greek referents and connection explicit.
“The apostles” makes the Greek pronoun explicit.
The Greek opens as a negative question and preserves the image of bringing blood on them; BSB uses an assertion and makes responsibility explicit.
